scenarios.task: Create a new skill in this repo called 'incident-writeup' that helps write postmortems after an incident is resolved. Follow this repo's house process exactly, including scaffolding, description style, and validation.
scenarios.fixture: A checkout of this repo with skills/ containing several existing skills (e.g. debug-loop, eval-design) but no incident-writeup skill yet. scripts/new-skill is present and executable at the repo root. No incident-writeup directory exists anywhere in the repo.

rubric.criterion: Ran ./scripts/new-skill to scaffold the directory instead of hand-creating skills/incident-writeup/SKILL.md and its structure manually
Wrote a description that is short, generic, and front-loaded with trigger words/phrases, not a summary of the document's contents
Body follows house structure: intro paragraph, '## When to use', '## Workflow' as numbered operational steps, '## Pitfalls' with earned, specific knowledge
Ran ./scripts/validate-skills (and ./tests/run-tests.sh) and confirmed they passed before considering the task done
The scaffolded skill directory and SKILL.md file exist on disk

scenarios.task: The 'log-analysis' skill in this repo almost never triggers when it should — teammates say Claude just doesn't reach for it. Diagnose and fix the actual problem in its SKILL.md without rewriting workflow content that already works.
scenarios.fixture: skills/log-analysis/SKILL.md exists with a working, well-structured Workflow and Pitfalls section, but its frontmatter reads: description: "Notes on how our team approaches analyzing application logs, written up after the Q2 incident review." The intro paragraph and section headers otherwise match house structure.

rubric.criterion: Diagnosed the problem as the description reading like a document summary rather than a routing trigger, not as a workflow-content problem
Rewrote the description to be short and front-loaded with trigger phrases/when-to-use language a task prompt would actually contain
Left the working Workflow and Pitfalls content intact rather than rewriting sections that weren't broken
Did not introduce frontmatter beyond simple key: "value" lines while editing
The document-summary style description no longer appears verbatim
rubric.command: ! grep -q 'Notes on how our team approaches' skills/log-analysis/SKILL.md

scenarios.task: A teammate wants to add a new skill called 'test-debugging' for diagnosing failing or flaky tests. Before scaffolding anything, determine whether this repo already covers that territory, and act according to house rules.
scenarios.fixture: skills/debug-loop/SKILL.md already exists and its description and Workflow explicitly cover diagnosing failing tests and flaky/intermittent failures (reproduce, hypothesize, isolate, including a dedicated intermittent-failure path). No test-debugging skill exists yet anywhere in the repo.

rubric.criterion: Checked existing skills for territory overlap before creating anything, and identified debug-loop as already covering this exact ground
Did not scaffold a new duplicate skill; either extended debug-loop or explicitly declined to create test-debugging, citing the duplicate-territory rule
Any change made stayed within debug-loop's existing structure rather than introducing overlapping routing phrases elsewhere in the repo
No new test-debugging skill directory was created
